recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core follow-up is needed for FHIR-34874; any future context changes for patient-proficiency should be made in the FHIR Extension Pack source.
issue_request: FHIR-34874 asked to broaden the patient-proficiency extension so proficiency can be represented for practitioner communication. The final Jira resolution required adding practitioner.communication and explicitly declined healthcareservice.communication and practitionerrole.communication because those represent advertised service or role language capability rather than an individual's proficiency.
initial_application: The current HL7/fhir core checkout does not define StructureDefinition/patient-proficiency because extension definitions were removed from the R5 core source. The applicable change was applied in the FHIR Extension Pack by commit 8cb6561b118b30ad5e942862da75b2475305f850, which added Practitioner.communication to input/definitions/multiple/StructureDefinition-patient-proficiency.xml.
additional_context: The current Extension Pack source lists Patient.communication, RelatedPerson.communication, Practitioner.communication, and Person.communication contexts, with no HealthcareService.communication or PractitionerRole.communication context. Current core source still builds Practitioner, PractitionerRole, and HealthcareService, and Practitioner.communication now points implementers to patient-proficiency through a later FHIR-47305 comment update.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit on the combined core branch. No HL7/fhir source change is appropriate because the target extension source is maintained outside this checkout and already reflects the Jira resolution.

related_jiras.note: Later Applied issue confirms patient-proficiency is the intended Practitioner.communication proficiency mechanism and added the current core comment pointing to it.

Practitioner communication restructuring context helps explain why PractitionerRole.communication and HealthcareService.communication advertise patient-facing language capability rather than personal proficiency.
